newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond volatility sticks below 9 percent.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond volatility sticks below 9 percent.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond futures fell back to contract lows Friday after the market digested the week's biggest economic numbers, the March producer price index and retail sales.
However, June bond volatility finished the session up from Thursday as values were adjusted for weekend time decay, bond floor analysts said.

Using Monday's date, floor analysts quoted June volatility at 8.95 percent after the close. That was up from 8.75 percent on the opening and 8.50 percent at midmorning, after the economic numbers were released.
Volatility for June options dipped below 9.00 percent for the first time last week after trading between 9.00 and 10.00 percent since mid-January, one floor analyst said.
By holding below the recent range, volatility shows that the bond market remains comfortable in a downtrend and unconcerned about a violent price swing, the analyst said.

June bond futures slid to a fresh seven-month low Friday after core producer prices excluding food and energy rose 0.4 percent in March. Overall, PPI was down 0.1 percent. Upward revisions to January and February retail sales provided more fodder for the bears.

The two-way order flow in options saw a decent number of puts change hands, floor sources said. Several speculative trades focused on cheap out-of-the-money May options, which expire next week. One of the largest involved the purchase of 2,500 May 108 calls.
Trade in 10-year note options was also brisk, with 1,000- and 2,000-lot transactions common, and a U.S. banking firm's purchase of 3,000 June 105 puts was the standout.
In Eurodollar options, volatility was steady to higher, with June unchanged at 7.50 percent and September flat at 10.20 percent.
December Euro volatility edged up 0.2 point to 12.00 percent, March was steady at 13.00 percent, June 1998 rose 0.2 point to 14.30 percent and September 1998 was steady at 15.20 percent.
Short-dated mid-curve options volatility waa steady at 15.60 percent in June 1998 and up 0.3 point to 15.80 percent in September 1998.
